lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice translating short scheduling sentences with time adverbials and natural Swedish word order.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Sending a concise message about arriving, waiting, and meeting later.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Writing and saying short practical updates without English word order.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik exchange short updates about arrival time, waiting, and a practical meeting point.

main_focus.name: time adverbials in practical updates
main_focus.description: Use phrases such as i morgon, senare, först, and efter lunch at the start or middle of a main clause with correct word order.
model_examples: I morgon kommer jag lite senare.
Jag kommer lite senare i morgon.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use time adverbials naturally 4-5 times, with at least two sentence-initial examples.

avoid_grammar: preteritum versus perfekt as the main focus

vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Prioritize reusable chunks that can appear in text messages and spoken updates.

dialogue_shape.opening: One person sends or mentions a short update about arriving later.
dialogue_shape.middle: They clarify waiting time, meeting place, and whether another message is needed.
dialogue_shape.ending: They agree to check in again or meet at the confirmed place.

target_complexity.repetition: repeat time adverbials in slightly different sentence positions

focus: what action is needed while waiting
what follow-up or meeting arrangement is agreed

sentence_focus: one sentence starting with i morgon
one sentence with efter lunch in first position
one question with kan du vänta
one sentence about sending a message
one sentence confirming where and when to meet
